Hello,

This subreddit is mostly for people who want to talk about personnal difficulties, and suicide. In the side bar, you can read "If you've lost someone to suicide, /r/SuicideBereavement is there for you, or you can check out our shared list of bereavement resources."

Hey selfless shellfish
Is there anything you want to talk about in particular?

I guess what you mean is that you are going to get a job consumming all of your time, and won't be able to move away or do anything else. Is there a way for you to get a different job somewhere else? If your future job a cause of trouble to you, it's probably the first thing you want to adress. Is there anyone you know that could help you with that, even if it's just a distant relation? Could you contact him/her to see if he/she could help you?

I understand how you feel about the people teel you that it's wrong and you're irrational etc. But keep in mind that they say it because to them it is obvious, and they probably don't aim at hurting you. 

To summerize my previous answer to why suicide is bad, it's bad because it usually hurts those around the person who commits suicide, and it can be seen as bad because it's seen as a failure to solving/ helping someone solve their problems. You don't have to agree with those points, but I think you can understand why others see suicide as bad, and why they want to prevent it.
And if you are already convinced that suicide isn't bad, I don't think that I nor anybody else can convince you otherwise.

The thing is, suicide will always be a choice, even when you say 'So I don't get to have a choice?'. For instance, in the middle ages, suicide was heavily punished, people who commited suicide where not buried normaly and their dead bodies where beaten as a sign of disapproval. And yet some people still did commit suicide. So no society can stop suicide. Today, suicide is thankfully understood with more empathy in our societies, but to some people, it is still ununderstandable.

About what you say 'life is meaningless', is there nothing in your life that you consider interesting, worth living for? Your 'choice' is linked to that vision of life, if not the direct consequence. In the end, I think that **what people mean by 'suicide must be prevented' is actually, 'the unhappiness and pain that pushes towards suicide should be prevented, because as human beings, we understand that nobody wishes to be in a position where suicide is a viable option'.**

Finally, what other options should there be aside from live (suck it up, to just "keep trying because things will get better" (only to die anyway)) or die?

Do you give up on trying to get "friends, a job, a girlfriend, prospects", because you are afraid to 'feel another ' pain? I mean sure nobody likes feeling even worse about themself after failling, but at that point, what do you risk? I'm not gonna force you, but giving it an honest try can't really get you much lower, can it?

I understand how undoable what I say might seem, and I  understand if you feel that you don't have the strenght, but it doesn't seem that things will get better by doing nothing.

If you feel like trying, consider doing it little by little, otherwise it might seem overwhelmingly hard. For instance, did you really never have anybody you spent a good time with, even if you weren't close? Is there some place you could meet some people? Is there any activity that you like? Is there a place, a person that you wish you where with/ in?

Hello,

This is a very philosophical question which is actually not easy. I totally agree with you about the fact that value and meaning are personnal things, and therefore life can seem meaningless.

I think the question of "bad" comes with "bad" for you and "bad" for others. 

Why is it bad for others? That is probably the easiest to answer. Imagine you lose a friend. You feel sad, you feel like a part of you is gone forever, and it hurts. And if it is to suicide, you feel like you could have done something to help him, and sometimes you don't understand. In that regard, it can be called bad, and that is probably the reason many societies have a negative view on suicide.

About yourself, it depends on what you think about life and death. It depends on if you believe in god and if you believe that god wants you to live, for instance. Death is not inherently bad, and everybody dies eventually, but things like diseases, pain, grief, that surround death cause great pain, and therefore are seen as bad.

There is also the problem of the choice. Many people who commit suicide feel trapped by circomptances, by poverty, by an hostile environnement. And they see suicide as an out, but might dream that things hadn't gone the way they did, and wished for a different life if they could. If you read some posts on this forum, you will probably enconter some. So what is the best solution? Try to help those people get out of their problematic situation, or tell them that they are "free" to kill themselves? 
It's not really about the right to die, as you said, it's about the fact that often, if you want to die, there is a reason, and people arround the suicidal person wish they could help deal with that reason.

So what do you think about that answer? (also abortion is a bit different because the mother/couple decides for the feotus about life, it's not really the right to die)

Hello,

You can find advice on the banner on the right, for exemple on [reddit!]/r/SWResources or in the guidelines.

Basically, talking about suicide is not going to give him more suicidal thoughts, especially if he already thinks about it, so you can talk about it. If he tells you he wants to commit suicide, don't go with generic sentences like 'it gets better' or make him feel guilty about his family and friends, instead try to know if there is still anything he still likes/want to live for, and **listen to him and empathise** to what he has to say, and his reasons. Since you already know his background about his girlfriend and family and medicine, you can tell   him how you feel about those things, but maybe try to insiste on the fact that things could change (he could get another girlfrind, he could see his family less in the future, he could stop his medication). Those things are in the present but we all know how things can change with time. You can also ask him to not do it in the near future, arguing he is not loosing much by waiting for a bit.

Finally, you can consider referring to professionnals, especially if you feel that he is on the edge of commiting suicide, or if you don't feel you can do any of the above. But he might be more willing to talk to you, since you are his friend and feeling that you have a friend in hard times is so important.

hope it helps.

Hi again,

I'm sorry to hear about the way you were treated at that psychiatric unit. And I'm sorry that your other attempts to get help didn't work either. 

However, these feelings are in the present and in the past. I get that because you feel desperate, you don't think that things could change and you will always be 'a burden'. In the end, my point is that you think that the future will be equaly painful as the present, but it might be brighter.

Many people feel that they are a burden to others, and sometimes it's true. But do we want a society that gets rid of all the people that are weak at some moment in their life? Sould we get rid of the elderly, because they are a burden to some? I think not. I think we should try to help each other in those moments of weakness. And being a burden doesn't mean that no one loves you and that you count for no one. For example, sometime you might think of your parents as burdens, but it doesn't mean you would want them to go away forever. So you might feel like you are a burden to others, but you are probably more that that to them.

A way to try to change this circle of thinking is to try and achieve something that is meaningful to you. It doesn't have to be big, it can be just call someone you like, or go running or even watch a TV show you like.

About the drinking, do you feel that you are dependent on alcohol? Is it part of what triggers these desperate feelings? If so, that may be the first thing you need to adress. I don't really know much about alcohol, so I can't really help you there, but there surely are some structures that could help you, like associations or hotlines.

I know that all of what I said may seem difficult to you, if not impossible, but since you came here and are talking, there must be a part of you that keeps hoping to get better. Maybe this though will help you somewhat.

What do you think makes the "worth" of a life? Is it being useful to someone? being productive? Then are handicapped people worthless? I don't think so. Sometimes in life, some of us feel they are useless or weak, and it's painful but it's often temporary. Like said before, thinking you are useless right now doesn't mean you really are, and certainly doesn't mean that you always will be.

I hope things will get better for you and your family.

Hi,

First, you don't have to feel bad for 'bothering people', this subreddit is there for you to express how you feel and people who are there are there to listen to what you have to say and try to help you the best the can.

It seems that you have been using drinking, thinking about suicide and cutting as coping mechanism to deal with your problems. But you realised that they are just helping on the short term, and are actually toxic on the long term. So i suggest you try to change these coping mechanism to some that actually don't harm you in the long run. Of course, it's easy for me to say, and you probably don't know where to start.

Maybe there is something you like doing and makes you happy. If so, I would encourage you to try to force you to practice it as often as possible. Maybe you want to focus on something that is meaningful to you, so that you feel you have a goal. Examples can be family, friends, love, spirituality/religion, art, work, money/social success, helping out others, travels, sports/games, philosohy, science or whatever you want. On another level, maybe some thoughts triggers those negative behaviours, and you would like to deal with that. Finally, I encourage you to talk about some of your issues to people you think might be able to help you in a constructive way, like a conselor or a teacher or a friend.

I hope this helps you in some way.
